audit_status.source_base: Greek Acts text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Paul before Agrippa, Pharisee hope, persecution accountability, Damascus commission, light to nations, Festus interruption, Agrippa response.

verses.restored: Agrippa said to Paul, It is permitted for you to speak for yourself. Then Paul, stretching out the hand, began to defend himself:

familiar.text: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:

modern.text: Agrippa said to Paul, “You have permission to speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand and began his defense:

original.text: Ἀγρίππας δὲ πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον ἔφη· Ἐπιτρέπεταί σοι ⸀ὑπὲρ σεαυτοῦ λέγειν. τότε ὁ Παῦλος ⸂ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἀπελογεῖτο⸃·

verses.restored: Concerning all the things of which I am accused by Judeans, King Agrippa, I consider myself blessed to be about to defend myself before you today,

familiar.text: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:

modern.text: “King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to stand before you today to defend myself against all the accusations of the Jews,

original.text: Περὶ πάντων ὧν ἐγκαλοῦμαι ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, ἥγημαι ἐμαυτὸν μακάριον ἐπὶ σοῦ μέλλων ⸂σήμερον ἀπολογεῖσθαι⸃,

verses.restored: especially because you are knowledgeable of all customs and questions among Judeans; therefore I ask you to hear me patiently.

familiar.text: Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.

modern.text: especially since you are acquainted with all the Jewish customs and controversies. I beg you, therefore, to listen to me patiently.

original.text: μάλιστα γνώστην ὄντα σε πάντων τῶν κατὰ Ἰουδαίους ⸀ἐθῶν τε καὶ ζητημάτων· διὸ ⸀δέομαι μακροθύμως ἀκοῦσαί μου.

verses.restored: My manner of life from youth, having been from the beginning among my nation and in Jerusalem, all Judeans know,

familiar.text: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;

modern.text: Surely all the Jews know how I have lived from the earliest days of my youth, among my own people and in Jerusalem.

original.text: Τὴν μὲν οὖν βίωσίν μου ⸀τὴν ἐκ νεότητος τὴν ἀπʼ ἀρχῆς γενομένην ἐν τῷ ἔθνει μου ἔν ⸀τε Ἱεροσολύμοις ἴσασι ⸀πάντες Ἰουδαῖοι,

verses.restored: having known me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that according to the strictest party of our religion, I lived as a Pharisee.

familiar.text: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.

modern.text: They have known me for a long time and can testify, if they are willing, that I lived as a Pharisee, adhering to the strictest sect of our religion.

original.text: προγινώσκοντές με ἄνωθεν, ἐὰν θέλωσι μαρτυρεῖν, ὅτι κατὰ τὴν ἀκριβεστάτην αἵρεσιν τῆς ἡμετέρας θρησκείας ἔζησα Φαρισαῖος.

verses.restored: And now I stand being judged for hope in the promise made by the Divine to our fathers,

familiar.text: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers:

modern.text: And now I stand on trial because of my hope in the promise that God made to our fathers,

original.text: καὶ νῦν ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι τῆς ⸀εἰς τοὺς πατέρας ⸀ἡμῶν ἐπαγγελίας γενομένης ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἕστηκα κρινόμενος,

verses.restored: to which our twelve tribes, earnestly serving night and day, hope to arrive. Concerning this hope I am accused by Judeans, O king.

familiar.text: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope’s sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.

modern.text: the promise our twelve tribes are hoping to realize as they earnestly serve God day and night. It is because of this hope, O king, that I am accused by the Jews.

original.text: εἰς ἣν τὸ δωδεκάφυλον ἡμῶν ἐν ἐκτενείᾳ νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν λατρεῦον ἐλπίζει καταντῆσαι· περὶ ἧς ἐλπίδος ἐγκαλοῦμαι ⸂ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων, βασιλεῦ⸃·

verses.restored: Why is it judged unbelievable among you if the Divine raises dead ones?

familiar.text: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?

modern.text: Why would any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?

original.text: τί ἄπιστον κρίνεται παρʼ ὑμῖν εἰ ὁ θεὸς νεκροὺς ἐγείρει;

verses.restored: I myself therefore thought it necessary to do many opposing things against the name of Jesus the Nazarene.

familiar.text: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

modern.text: So then, I too was convinced that I ought to do all I could to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

original.text: Ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν ἔδοξα ἐμαυτῷ πρὸς τὸ ὄνομα Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου δεῖν πολλὰ ἐναντία πρᾶξαι·

verses.restored: This I also did in Jerusalem; many of the holy ones I locked in prisons, receiving authority from the chief priests, and when they were being killed, I cast my vote against them.

familiar.text: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.

modern.text: And that is what I did in Jerusalem. With authority from the chief priests I put many of the saints in prison, and when they were condemned to death, I cast my vote against them.

original.text: ὃ καὶ ἐποίησα ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις, καὶ πολλούς ⸀τε τῶν ἁγίων ἐγὼ ⸀ἐν φυλακαῖς κατέκλεισα τὴν παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων ἐξουσίαν λαβών, ἀναιρουμένων τε αὐτῶν κατήνεγκα ψῆφον,

verses.restored: Punishing them often throughout all the synagogues, I tried to compel them to blaspheme; being exceedingly enraged against them, I pursued them even to cities outside.

familiar.text: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.

modern.text: I frequently had them punished in the synagogues, and I tried to make them blaspheme. In my raging fury against them, I even went to foreign cities to persecute them.

original.text: καὶ κατὰ πάσας τὰς συναγωγὰς πολλάκις τιμωρῶν αὐτοὺς ἠνάγκαζον βλασφημεῖν, περισσῶς τε ἐμμαινόμενος αὐτοῖς ἐδίωκον ἕως καὶ εἰς τὰς ἔξω πόλεις.

verses.restored: In these things, journeying to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,

familiar.text: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,

modern.text: In this pursuit I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.

original.text: Ἐν ⸀οἷς πορευόμενος εἰς τὴν Δαμασκὸν μετʼ ἐξουσίας καὶ ἐπιτροπῆς ⸀τῆς τῶν ἀρχιερέων

verses.restored: at midday on the road, O king, I saw from heaven a light beyond the brightness of the sun shining around me and those journeying with me.

familiar.text: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.

modern.text: About noon, O king, as I was on the road, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and my companions.

original.text: ἡμέρας μέσης κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν εἶδον, βασιλεῦ, οὐρανόθεν ὑπὲρ τὴν λαμπρότητα τοῦ ἡλίου περιλάμψαν με φῶς καὶ τοὺς σὺν ἐμοὶ πορευομένους·

verses.restored: When we all had fallen to the ground, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew dialect, Saul, Saul, why do you pursue me? It is hard for you to kick against goads.

familiar.text: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.

modern.text: We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice say to me in Hebrew, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’

original.text: πάντων ⸀τε καταπεσόντων ἡμῶν εἰς τὴν γῆν ἤκουσα φωνὴν ⸀λέγουσαν πρός ⸀με τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ· Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις; σκληρόν σοι πρὸς κέντρα λακτίζειν.

verses.restored: I said, Who are you, Lord? The Lord said, I am Jesus, whom you pursue.

familiar.text: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.

modern.text: ‘Who are You, Lord?’ I asked. ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,’ the Lord replied.

original.text: ἐγὼ δὲ εἶπα· Τίς εἶ, κύριε; ὁ δὲ ⸀κύριος εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὃν σὺ διώκεις·

verses.restored: But rise and stand upon your feet; for to this I appeared to you, to appoint you as servant and witness both of what you have seen and of what I will show you,

familiar.text: But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;

modern.text: ‘But get up and stand on your feet. For I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and as a witness of what you have seen from Me and what I will show you.

original.text: ἀλλὰ ἀνάστηθι καὶ στῆθι ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας σου· εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ὤφθην σοι, προχειρίσασθαί σε ὑπηρέτην καὶ μάρτυρα ὧν τε εἶδές ⸀με ὧν τε ὀφθήσομαί σοι,

verses.restored: rescuing you from the people and from the nations, to whom I send you,

familiar.text: Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,

modern.text: I will rescue you from your own people and from the Gentiles. I am sending you to them

original.text: ἐξαιρούμενός σε ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ⸀ἐκ τῶν ἐθνῶν, εἰς οὓς ἐγὼ ⸂ἀποστέλλω σε⸃

verses.restored: to open their eyes, to turn them from darkness to light and from the authority of the adversarial one to the Divine, so that they may receive release of sins/misalignments and inheritance among those sanctified by trust in me.

familiar.text: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.

modern.text: to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those sanctified by faith in Me.’

original.text: ἀνοῖξαι ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν, τοῦ ⸀ἐπιστρέψαι ἀπὸ σκότους εἰς φῶς καὶ τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ Σατανᾶ ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν, τοῦ λαβεῖν αὐτοὺς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν καὶ κλῆρον ἐν τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις πίστει τῇ εἰς ἐμέ.

verses.restored: Therefore, King Agrippa, I did not become disobedient to the heavenly vision,

familiar.text: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:

modern.text: So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.

original.text: Ὅθεν, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, οὐκ ἐγενόμην ἀπειθὴς τῇ οὐρανίῳ ὀπτασίᾳ,

verses.restored: but first to those in Damascus, and also Jerusalem, and all the region of Judea, and to the nations, I was announcing that they should turn/realign and return to the Divine, doing works worthy of turning.

familiar.text: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.

modern.text: First to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, then to everyone in the region of Judea, and then to the Gentiles, I declared that they should repent and turn to God, performing deeds worthy of their repentance.

original.text: ἀλλὰ τοῖς ἐν Δαμασκῷ πρῶτόν ⸀τε καὶ Ἱεροσολύμοις, ⸀πᾶσάν τε τὴν χώραν τῆς Ἰουδαίας, καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ⸀ἀπήγγελλον μετανοεῖν καὶ ἐπιστρέφειν ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν, ἄξια τῆς μετανοίας ἔργα πράσσοντας.

verses.restored: Because of these things, Judeans seized me in the temple and were attempting to kill me.

familiar.text: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me.

modern.text: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple courts and tried to kill me.

original.text: ἕνεκα τούτων ⸂με Ἰουδαῖοι⸃ ⸀συλλαβόμενοι ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἐπειρῶντο διαχειρίσασθαι.

verses.restored: Therefore, obtaining help from the Divine until this day, I stand bearing witness to small and great, saying nothing except what the prophets and Moses said was about to happen:

familiar.text: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:

modern.text: But I have had God’s help to this day, and I stand here to testify to small and great alike. I am saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen:

original.text: ἐπικουρίας οὖν τυχὼν τῆς ⸀ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἄχρι τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης ἕστηκα μαρτυρόμενος μικρῷ τε καὶ μεγάλῳ, οὐδὲν ἐκτὸς λέγων ὧν τε οἱ προφῆται ἐλάλησαν μελλόντων γίνεσθαι καὶ Μωϋσῆς,

verses.restored: that the Messiah was to suffer, that being first from resurrection of the dead, he was about to announce light both to the people and to the nations.

familiar.text: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.

modern.text: that the Christ would suffer, and as the first to rise from the dead, would proclaim light to our people and to the Gentiles.” Festus Interrupts Paul’s Defense

original.text: εἰ παθητὸς ὁ χριστός, εἰ πρῶτος ἐξ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν φῶς μέλλει καταγγέλλειν τῷ ⸀τε λαῷ καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν.

verses.restored: As he was saying these things in defense, Festus says with a great voice, Paul, you are mad; much learning is turning you to madness.

familiar.text: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.

modern.text: At this stage of Paul’s defense, Festus exclaimed in a loud voice, “You are insane, Paul! Your great learning is driving you to madness!”

original.text: Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀπολογουμένου ὁ Φῆστος μεγάλῃ τῇ φωνῇ ⸀φησιν· Μαίνῃ, Παῦλε· τὰ πολλά σε γράμματα εἰς μανίαν περιτρέπει.

verses.restored: But Paul says, I am not mad, most excellent Festus, but I speak words of truth and sober-mindedness.

familiar.text: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.

modern.text: But Paul answered, “I am not insane, most excellent Festus; I am speaking words of truth and sobriety.

original.text: ὁ δὲ ⸀Παῦλος· Οὐ μαίνομαι, φησίν, κράτιστε Φῆστε, ἀλλὰ ἀληθείας καὶ σωφροσύνης ῥήματα ἀποφθέγγομαι.

verses.restored: For the king knows about these things, to whom I also speak boldly; for I am persuaded none of these things is hidden from him, for this has not been done in a corner.

familiar.text: For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.

modern.text: For the king knows about these matters, and I can speak freely to him. I am confident that none of this has escaped his notice, because it was not done in a corner.

original.text: ἐπίσταται γὰρ περὶ τούτων ὁ βασιλεύς, πρὸς ὃν ⸀καὶ παρρησιαζόμενος λαλῶ· λανθάνειν γὰρ ⸀αὐτὸν τούτων οὐ πείθομαι ⸀οὐθέν, οὐ γάρ ⸀ἐστιν ἐν γωνίᾳ πεπραγμένον τοῦτο.

verses.restored: King Agrippa, do you trust the prophets? I know that you trust.

familiar.text: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.

modern.text: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do.”

original.text: πιστεύεις, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, τοῖς προφήταις; οἶδα ὅτι πιστεύεις.

verses.restored: Agrippa said to Paul, In a little, are you persuading me to become Christian?

familiar.text: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.

modern.text: Then Agrippa said to Paul, “Can you persuade me in such a short time to become a Christian?”

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἀγρίππας πρὸς τὸν ⸀Παῦλον· Ἐν ὀλίγῳ με πείθεις Χριστιανὸν ⸀ποιῆσαι.

verses.restored: Paul said, I would pray to the Divine, whether in little or in much, not only you but also all those hearing me today might become such as I am, except for these bonds.

familiar.text: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only thou, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.

modern.text: “Short time or long,” Paul replied, “I wish to God that not only you but all who hear me this day may become what I am, except for these chains.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ ⸀Παῦλος· Εὐξαίμην ἂν τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐν ὀλίγῳ καὶ ἐν ⸀μεγάλῳ οὐ μόνον σὲ ἀλλὰ καὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντάς μου σήμερον γενέσθαι τοιούτους ὁποῖος καὶ ἐγώ εἰμι παρεκτὸς τῶν δεσμῶν τούτων.

verses.restored: The king rose, and the governor, and Bernice, and those sitting with them.

familiar.text: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:

modern.text: Then the king and the governor rose, along with Bernice and those seated with them.

original.text: ⸀Ἀνέστη ⸀τε ὁ βασιλεὺς καὶ ὁ ἡγεμὼν ἥ τε Βερνίκη καὶ οἱ συγκαθήμενοι αὐτοῖς,

verses.restored: Withdrawing, they were speaking to one another, saying, This human does nothing worthy of death or bonds.

familiar.text: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.

modern.text: On their way out, they said to one another, “This man has done nothing worthy of death or imprisonment.”

original.text: καὶ ἀναχωρήσαντες ἐλάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους λέγοντες ὅτι Οὐδὲν θανάτου ⸂ἢ δεσμῶν ἄξιον⸃ ⸀τι πράσσει ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος.

verses.restored: Agrippa said to Festus, This human could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.

familiar.text: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Caesar.

modern.text: And Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.”

original.text: Ἀγρίππας δὲ τῷ Φήστῳ ἔφη· Ἀπολελύσθαι ἐδύνατο ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος εἰ μὴ ἐπεκέκλητο Καίσαρα.
